# 2 Baruch Chapter 44 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** Third Fast and Vision

---

**1** I, Baruch, spoke up and addressed the elders:

**2** "Listen, all you elders. Pay attention, all of you who are gathered here.

**3** You know how our ancestors abandoned the law in earlier times — and because of that, disaster fell on them and on us.

**4** But the hope of those who have kept the commandments of the Mighty One will never fail. Their reward will remain even when all the ages have run out.

**5** The time of this world will pass away. Its glory will fade. Everything beautiful in it will turn to dust. The proud will be as though they never existed.

**6** Those who put their trust in wealth will be like people who have already died. Those who lord it over others will cry out in grief and be disgraced.

**7** The things that are coming are of immense value and greatness. The things that are passing away are small and brief.

**8** Everyone who has hoped in the Anointed One who was coming — they will live in joy. But those who were not counted among the people who truly know God — they will be destroyed.

**9** The hope of those who trusted the law from their hearts will never perish. It will never fail.

**10** But how long will this world's lamp burn? When will this darkness that now covers everything be extinguished?

**11** Why does the beauty of the earth keep growing old? Why must its strength decay? When will the Mighty One himself come in glory to judge all who live on the earth?"

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering of Baruch's great address. The contrast between fading world and eternal hope is the rhetorical climax. The questions at the end (vv.10-11) echo the lament of ch. 21, creating a structural echo in the book.*
